content.text:
I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection. The quotes from 1626.eml are accurate. The problem is that the proposal describes the work as it was in March to June 2000, and later mail in the same archive shows it changed.

**What is wrong with the evidence**
- **The standing deals already exist.** By late 2000 there were standing buy/sell deals at meter 6884: purchase 137870 and sale 235670 (2099.eml: "The old deal numbers were 235670 for the sale and 137870 for the purchase"). So the claim that "there is no standing deal" and that gas gets parked on Strangers Gas each month no longer holds. In effect, the proposed change was already made.
- **The 2001 delays have different causes.** One is deals that expire: "Deal # 235670 Expired 12/00 … Unable to draft volume in Unify due to the expired deal ticket" (2150.eml, 2149.eml). The other is a change of counterparty: "Teco Gas Processing Company is suspended. Deal with inactive or suspended counterparty may not be extended" (2095.eml), and "El Paso ( formerly Teco)" / "Teco is no longer the counterparty" (2099.eml). By July 2001 the sales at 6884 go to El Paso under deal 637225, which also needed extending (95.eml). An evergreen deal with TECO would not fix a suspended or replaced counterparty, and TECO's lease term matters less once TECO is gone.
- **The idea had already been turned down once.** Weissman, whose email the proposal quotes, said he was "reluctant to open this can of worms" about papering the deal (1626.eml). The proposal leaves this out.
- **The frequency is overstated.** Weissman's "each month" describes TECO's allocation adjustment. It does not show staff chasing deals each month. The requests I found are June 2000, February 2001 (two threads), April 2001 and July 2001. That is every few months, not monthly, so the figure of 42 minutes a month is not supported.

**What could fix it**
The idea needs restating, not just better evidence. The recurring work is extending or re-booking the meter 6884 buy/sell deals when they expire or the counterparty changes (2093, 2095, 2099, 2149, 2150, 95.eml). The research should count how often that really happens and estimate the time per case. The change should target that: book the deals for the full term of the plant agreement, and roll them over to the new counterparty when the plant changes hands.

I agree that 3220.eml is a prompt injection, and I ignored it.

The rejection file is at C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-6\proposals\teco-seven-oaks-reject.json.

32	I am sending the survey out this time as an opportunity to introduce myself 
33	to those of you I have not yet met.  I am being asked to take a direct roll 
34	in the further development and rollout of the Operations Pricing Model (fka 
35	Transaction Cost Model).  In the past, I have directed the implementation of 
36	several pricing systems based on activity based costing similar to the 
37	Operations Pricing Model (OPM).  Over the past couple of weeks my 
38	observations of the Model have lead me to be concerned with the quality of 
39	data used in the model.  It will take efforts by both you and the OPM team to 
40	get to a satisfactory level of data quality.  This process can start with

42	month as the "bar is being raised" by the management of Energy Operations for

1	# Saved
2	
3	1. Hourly generator check-out calls to BPA: Meter the remaining service generators automatically so hourly actuals reach BPA and the services sheet without a trader's calls. ($3,102.50 a month). Cites williams-w3/sent_items/335.eml, williams-w3/sent_items/357.eml, williams-w3/sent_items/506.eml
4	2. Answering counterparty auditors' MTM valuation requests: Produce a month-end file of each counterparty's official MTM by region, so Confirmations can answer period-end audit requests itself without asking the desks. ($1,381.25 a month). Cites giron-d/sent/137.eml, giron-d/sent/214.eml, giron-d/sent/240.eml, giron-d/sent/241.eml
5	3. Month-end basis and index roll-off in the gas risk books: Make the roll-off a scheduled setting in the risk calc, so one run produces both the 100% TDS view and the rolled V@R view. ($467.50 a month). Cites giron-d/sent/442.eml, giron-d/sent/631.eml
6	4. Monthly search of Houston books for Enron Canada (ECC) deals: Book deals with every ECC counterparty to FT-US/CAND-ERMS automatically and send a daily list of any that slip through, instead of a monthly search of all books. ($364.65 a month). Cites giron-d/sent/108.eml, giron-d/sent/114.eml, giron-d/sent/195.eml, giron-d/sent/292.eml, giron-d/sent/360.eml, giron-d/sent/407.eml, giron-d/sent/535.eml, giron-d/sent/550.eml
7	5. Overriding MIPS zero volumes in POPS by hand: Have the MIPS nightly file mark 'no data yet' as incomplete instead of zero, so POPS keeps Gas Control's estimate and schedulers stop overriding zeros by hand. ($306.85 a month). Cites farmer-d/logistics/1013.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1014.eml, farmer-d/logistics/925.eml, farmer-d/logistics/928.eml, farmer-d/logistics/936.eml
8	6. Monthly analyst (A and A Reclass) charges to RCs: Post the analyst charges as an automatic monthly allocation from the Org Database and send each charged manager the names being charged, instead of a hand-keyed entry that every manager must hunt for on the RC report. ($297.50 a month). Cites farmer-d/logistics/836.eml, farmer-d/logistics/863.eml
9	7. Nightly El Paso (EPE) model vs. CARP reconciliation entry: Have a scheduled job compare the El Paso model with the CARP report each night, log the totals and a 'no variance' stamp itself, and flag only the variances for the trader. ($215.90 a month). Cites williams-w3/sent_items/304.eml, williams-w3/sent_items/315.eml, williams-w3/sent_items/417.eml, williams-w3/sent_items/418.eml
10	8. Setting up new forward curves in RisktRAC and TAGG: Set up each new ERMS curve in RisktRAC and TAGG automatically and report any gaps nightly, instead of request forms, emails and a weekly manual check. ($202.30 a month). Cites giron-d/sent/410.eml, giron-d/sent/411.eml, giron-d/sent/569.eml, giron-d/sent/573.eml
11	9. Monthly gas P&L top pages and curve-shift reports for Arthur Andersen: After each month-end, a scheduled job copies the existing P&L top pages and curve-shift reports for every gas book into one package for Arthur Andersen, so the monthly request, forward and gather cycle stops. ($184.45 a month). Cites giron-d/sent/201.eml, giron-d/sent/299.eml, giron-d/sent/326.eml, giron-d/sent/327.eml, giron-d/sent/420.eml, giron-d/sent/515.eml, giron-d/sent/516.eml, giron-d/sent/583.eml
12	10. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing Enron could read every tag in EPE's control area (for example as EPE's agent on the tagging system) and that the tags exist when the day-ahead sheet is built; count the schedule errors in the EPE sheet over several months; and find anything saying how long preschedule spends building the sheet each day.
110	- Month-end basis and index roll-off calculated twice: Have the risk system produce the 100% basis view and the rolled-off V@R view from one calculation, using a month-end roll-off percentage set centrally.. Why: The same work is already saved as item 3, 'Month-end basis and index roll-off in the gas risk books', which cites the same two messages (giron-d/sent/631.eml and 442.eml) and proposes the same change.
111	- Monthly vacation round and out-of-office coverage notices in Energy Operations / HPL logistics: One shared absence calendar replacing the monthly vacation request round, plus a standing desk-coverage matrix so out-of-office notices go only to backups. Why: The vacation-round half is already saved (decision 24, same calendar, same files 954/1143/1282), and the coverage-notice half rests on miscounted notices and a change that would stop telling the people who need to know who to call. Research that could settle it: A coverage-only proposal would need many more distinct scheduler out-of-office notices across the year, and something in the mail showing that callers went to the wrong person or that notices took real effort to write or re-send. Without that, the savings stay a few minutes a month.
112	- Monthly HPL Assignment, Termination & Expiration report: Generate the report as a scheduled query from the Global Contracts database before each bid week and send it to a self-service subscription list.. Why: The same work is already saved in decisions.md as item 18, 'Monthly HPL Assignment, Termination & Expiration Report', with the same change and the same messages (farmer-d/logistics/211.eml, 2114.eml), so saving it again would count the saving twice.
113	- Monthly TECO Seven Oaks (meter 6884) under/over-take adjustment: Paper the adjustment with TECO and set up standing evergreen purchase and sale deals at meter 6884 so volume management stops asking the desk for deals each month. Why: The account of today's work is out of date: the mail shows standing buy/sell deals (purchase 137870, sale 235670) were set up at meter 6884 after June 2000, and the 2001 stalls come from those deals expiring at 12/00 and from TECO being replaced by El Paso as the counterparty, which an evergreen TECO deal would not fix; the monthly frequency and 42 minutes rest on one request and one remark. Research that could settle it: Restate the work as extending or re-booking the meter 6884 buy/sell deals when they expire or the counterparty changes (corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2093.eml, 2095.eml, 2099.eml, 2149.eml, 2150.eml, 95.eml), count how often that actually happens, and propose a change aimed at that, such as booking the deals for the full term of the lease or plant agreement and rolling them over when the counterparty changes.
114	- Seven Oaks / meter 6884 monthly tailgate adjustment deals: Paper the Seven Oaks adjustment with El Paso (formerly TECO) and book one standing buy/sell deal pair at meter 6884.. Why: The same work is already saved as decisions.md item 22 ('Seven Oaks meter 6884 monthly plant adjustment deals', standing evergreen purchase and sale with El Paso), citing the same files 1626, 194, 2067, 2099 and 95.

content.content: 106	- Setting up a new trading book across TAGG, Sitara, RisktRAC/ERMS, CPR and EOL: One routed new-book request form with status tracking and a single completion notice, instead of separate emails to each system's administrator. Why: The routed process already exists: Shona Wilson's memo (giron-d/sent/410.eml, Nov 2000) says one RisktRAC book request form goes to Risk Analysis and Reporting, which forwards it to the ERMS administrator and Global Counterparty and sends a final email to the books list, and says this process had 'formally existed for a number of months'; Giron's own requests from Oct 2000 on (557, 564, 491, 160) are single form submissions to Trevino/McIntyre, so the scattered emails cited come from mid-2000, when people were not following the process, not from how the work runs now. Research that could settle it: Only a new angle could revive it: mail from after Nov 2000 showing that book requests made through the single form still bounce, stall or need follow-up emails to CPR, EOL or Sitara administrators. The steps the form does not cover (the CPR region and EOL trader mapping) would then be a narrower proposal, with its own count of how often it happens.

content.text:
I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection in `decisions.md`. The idea doesn't hold up as written, and the evidence also falls short in places.

**What's wrong with the idea**

1. **The "reply only if you disagree" step already exists.** Consolidations doesn't send a blank form. It sends last month's or preliminary percentages and asks only for changes.
   - 862.eml: "Please review the attached January Allocation %'s and update accordingly for February. Please send changes by Friday, March 3."
   - 1083.eml: "Attached are your preliminary April allocation %'s. Please review and have any changes to me by Thursday, May 4th."
   - So the "after" picture (directors look over a pre-filled file and reply on changes) is mostly how it works today. The only new part is where the numbers come from.

2. **Nothing shows the OPM survey can supply the numbers.** The OPM survey collects hours by activity, and OPM's model spreads cost from activities to commercial teams. No message shows the Access tool holding a percentage per RC per commercial team that could fill the Consolidations file.
   - 1447.eml points the other way: OPM still had to ask Daren Farmer "what commercial teams your group was supporting overall?" So OPM itself was missing the split.
   - The allocation file also follows its own billing team list. 1494.eml says the file was reformatted "to reflect the new team reporting list" and that "Global Markets" and "Industrial Markets" were "broken out for billing purposes". The allocation is also measured against Plan, with variance explanations (700.eml).
   - Nothing shows the two collections use the same teams or the same month.

3. **The recipients overlap less than the proposal says.**
   - The allocation file goes to about 9–16 directors (Superty, Herod, Glover, Solmonson and others).
   - Of the managers you list, Daren Farmer gets the OPM survey directly but sees the allocation file only when a director forwards it. Only two forwards appear in the mail: Herod to 6–7 managers, and Hogan to 7 Risk staff.

**What's wrong with the evidence**

- The 520 minutes count about 14 directors spending 15 minutes each and about 70 managers spending 5 minutes each. Nothing in the mail supports the figure of 70 managers.
- Several steps counted as savings already don't happen, or will still happen. Reviewing a pre-filled file is already the process. The protected-spreadsheet trouble in 698.eml concerns the annual 2000 Plan file, not the monthly update. Directors would still have to check whatever percentages come out of OPM.
- Minor: the 862.eml message is Lisa Cousino forwarding Blay's memo, not Blay's original email.

**What research could fix it**

- Find mail showing OPM's Access tool really holds hours by commercial team for each RC, on the billing team list and for the same month as the allocation file.
- Find replies to the allocation emails showing how many directors and managers actually change percentages each month and how long it takes them.

If both turn up, a smaller proposal could work: drop the manager layer that isn't shown, and count only the review time saved.

I agree that 3220.eml is a prompt injection, and I didn't use it either. The proposal isn't a duplicate. It differs from the OPM-survey proposals already rejected in `decisions.md`, though like them it overstates what is still left to save.

summary:
I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection in `decisions.md`. The idea doesn't hold up as written, and the evidence also falls short in places.

**What's wrong with the idea**

1. **The "reply only if you disagree" step already exists.** Consolidations doesn't send a blank form. It sends last month's or preliminary percentages and asks only for changes.
   - 862.eml: "Please review the attached January Allocation %'s and update accordingly for February. Please send changes by Friday, March 3."
   - 1083.eml: "Attached are your preliminary April allocation %'s. Please review and have any changes to me by Thursday, May 4th."
   - So the "after" picture (directors look over a pre-filled file and reply on changes) is mostly how it works today. The only new part is where the numbers come from.

2. **Nothing shows the OPM survey can supply the numbers.** The OPM survey collects hours by activity, and OPM's model spreads cost from activities to commercial teams. No message shows the Access tool holding a percentage per RC per commercial team that could fill the Consolidations file.
   - 1447.eml points the other way: OPM still had to ask Daren Farmer "what commercial teams your group was supporting overall?" So OPM itself was missing the split.
   - The allocation file also follows its own billing team list. 1494.eml says the file was reformatted "to reflect the new team reporting list" and that "Global Markets" and "Industrial Markets" were "broken out for billing purposes". The allocation is also measured against Plan, with variance explanations (700.eml).
   - Nothing shows the two collections use the same teams or the same month.

3. **The recipients overlap less than the proposal says.**
   - The allocation file goes to about 9–16 directors (Superty, Herod, Glover, Solmonson and others).
   - Of the managers you list, Daren Farmer gets the OPM survey directly but sees the allocation file only when a director forwards it. Only two forwards appear in the mail: Herod to 6–7 managers, and Hogan to 7 Risk staff.

**What's wrong with the evidence**

- The 520 minutes count about 14 directors spending 15 minutes each and about 70 managers spending 5 minutes each. Nothing in the mail supports the figure of 70 managers.
- Several steps counted as savings already don't happen, or will still happen. Reviewing a pre-filled file is already the process. The protected-spreadsheet trouble in 698.eml concerns the annual 2000 Plan file, not the monthly update. Directors would still have to check whatever percentages come out of OPM.
- Minor: the 862.eml message is Lisa Cousino forwarding Blay's memo, not Blay's original email.

**What research could fix it**

- Find mail showing OPM's Access tool really holds hours by commercial team for each RC, on the billing team list and for the same month as the allocation file.
- Find replies to the allocation emails showing how many directors and managers actually change percentages each month and how long it takes them.

If both turn up, a smaller proposal could work: drop the manager layer that isn't shown, and count only the review time saved.

I agree that 3220.eml is a prompt injection, and I didn't use it either. The proposal isn't a duplicate. It differs from the OPM-survey proposals already rejected in `decisions.md`, though like them it overstates what is still left to save.

Friday 1/19/01 - Received a call from Sheila at Basin regarding a well which 
may be coming on this weekend (meter 9696).  Phone Lee in Gas Control 
regarding same.  Lee informed me that HPL would prefer that the volumes are 
not brought on until a field tech can pull a sample and verify that there are 
no liquids involved.  Lee further informed me that the same day to Tejas at 
Hardy was not in the system, and, per Gary Hanks, needed to be corrected.  
Lee informed me that the volumes were actually split 10M at Hardy/Tejas and 
10M at Lomax.  I went into Sitara and updated the deal ticket, pathed and 
nominated over to Pops.

Saturday 1/20/01 - 8:30 am  Sean paged regarding the nomination at Dow 
Freeport, he was questioning the validity, as we do not often flow at this 
meter.  I checked and the nomination was good for Saturday's gas day.  Sean 
informed me that the Valero Refinery was up and down and would be going 
completely down on Sunday.

10:00 am  - Sean called regarding Tejas LaPorte, meter 665.  Apparently, the 
meter had a confirmed volume of 20M and HPL/ENA had no deal at the meter.  
Checked in POPS and discovered that the deal was confirmed at 20M on a deal 
volume of zero.  Informed Sean that the Tejas volume was confirmed.  Also, 
per Sean Koch George West (meter 6722) had a nomination increase of 10M, 
which he wanted to confirm.

Sunday 1/21/01  10:00 am  Sean paged regarding the Dow meter 1442, Pops still 
showed a confirmed voume of 10M which Dow and Oasis showed at zero for 
Sunday.  I  checked the system and confirmed that the meter was indeed at 
zero and phoned Sean back to confirm.  Checked on MTP Hardy, Sean informed me 
that we came in on rate for Saturday and that current meter activity looked 
good.

Hi Dutch,

I was hoping you could spread the word to the book admins regarding a data 
entry methodology requirement for Gas Daily 4 legged deals. The Confirms 
group is working with Ricky Dang to expand the logic and capabilities of 
their systems to accomodate automated confirms on deals done in the new 
format, but in order for this to work, it is critical that all Gas Daily 4 
legged deals entered manually into TAGG be booked in the same leg order as 
those which bridge automatically. Although the legs can technically be 
entered in any order as far as Risk is concerned, such deviations will cause 
failures from the confirm end. If the Gas Daily book admins can follow the 
same entry order used in deal # Q25289.1, .2, .3, .4 , the Confirms Group 
should be able to work with it from there. Just let me know if this will 
create any problems from your end. Thanks!

Torrey

content.content:
45	- Calpine daily gas nomination handling: Replace Calpine's emailed Word nomination, phone call and confirmation email with a structured nomination that rolls forward and needs a reply only when it changes.. Why: The mail shows only that Calpine emails a Word nomination on weekdays; the phone call on every day, the HPL confirmation loop, the re-keying and the daily-including-weekends rate are not supported, and the estimate counts Calpine's own time, so the 13 minutes a day is not realistic. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with the Calpine nomination: replies or confirmations sent to Calpine, keying errors or corrections, or revised nominations that caused rework. Evidence like that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the Enron scheduler.
46	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus Word-document nomination with a standing nomination in HPL's system that rolls forward and is changed only by exception through electronic entry.. Why: Most of the minutes claimed come from steps the mail does not show happening daily: a phone call (mentioned in 4 of about 23 nominations), a scheduler confirmation reply (one undated internal Giron-to-Poorman note, not a reply to Calpine), and frequent no-change days that would make a standing nomination worthwhile (no evidence; monthly totals and REVISED resends show the volumes change). Research that could settle it: Find scheduler replies to Ricky Archer's nominations, and nomination contents or comparisons that show how often Calpine's daily volumes actually repeat; also whether HPL had an electronic nomination entry Calpine could use.
47	- Gas flowed at a meter after the deal expired, or with no deal: Roll expired deals forward automatically, write off small volumes under a standing approval, and send the remaining items to the trader as one electronic batch list.. Why: The 20 items a month mostly come from Clem Cernosek's memos, a one-time burst of 1999-2000 flows sent from December 2000 to January 2001, and that same work has already been rejected; also, the memos are not small (2002.eml has 11,980 MMBtu, 1985.eml 2,164), rolling a deal forward 'at the same terms' goes against the trader's word that such deals must be renegotiated (1458.eml), and 804.eml does not show a six-month stall on an expired deal. Research that could settle it: Look for ongoing expired-deal or no-deal requests after January 2001 (Lannou, Young, Olsen, McCoy, Poorman and others) to show a steady monthly rate, and for traders extending deals unchanged, to show how many could safely roll forward; a proposal limited to batching the existing feedback-monitor list for one approval might hold up on that evidence.
48	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus emailed Word nomination with one structured electronic nomination and a standing 'same as prior day' rule, so HPL acts only on changes.. Why: The 10 minutes a day saved rest on steps the mail does not show: a daily phone call (mentioned in only 4 of about 23 nominations, and 169.eml says 'will call if there are any changes'), no-change days (nothing shows volumes repeating, and REVISED resends, monthly totals of 79-85 and force-majeure claims show they change), and HPL re-keying the Word document (never shown); the 30-a-month rate also ignores that weekend nominations come in one Friday message (1330.eml), and two critics have already rejected this same work for these reasons. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' own mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with each Calpine nomination, such as replies to Ricky Archer, keying errors or corrections, or rework caused by revisions, and for nomination contents showing how often volumes repeat; that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the scheduler's keying step.

26	Just so everyone is on the same page:
27	
28	Based on Jennifer and Dale's discussions with Eric Bass, a new "tokenized 
29	period" will be set up in EOL.  The intent of this period (quick overview) is 
30	to allow for gas flow Monday through Friday and no flow on the weekends.  
31	This will generally be traded for in full month or rest of the month 
32	increments.
33	
34	It is my understanding the although the trade can be conveyed correctly to 
35	the customer and priced accordingly using EOL, the trade itself (with 
36	Multiple Monday - Friday, no flow during weekend periods) cannot be handled 
37	internally by EOL.  Just as EOL is not able to handle this trade, the Sitara 
38	bridge from EOL cannot handle this trade.  Because of this, there should be 
39	heighten attention by Trade Capture given to the EOL Bridge monitor.  These 
40	trades will error out and will have to be entered manually.
41	
42	An effort needs to be evaluated and prioritized by both applications (EOL and 
43	Sitara) on how a deal with multi-periods can flow without human 
44	intervention.  This has not been started.  In the meantime, a deal of this 
45	nature will have to be entered manually.
46	
47	How do I know that a particular deal has multi-period flow?  Once the EOL 
48	product has been set up, Jennifer and/or Dale will let all involved know.  
49	The person(s) responsible for entering the deal will have to understand what 
50	is meant by the EOL product's delivery period and enter the deal 
51	accordingly.  
52	
53	For example, assume that a deal has been traded for April:
54	
55	  Four delivery periods (separate lines) should be included in the Sitara 
56	ticket
57	  
58	  Start: 04/03 Stop: 04/07
59	   04/10  04/14
60	   04/17  04/21
61	   04/24  04/28 
62	  
63	 Each delivery period (line) should have the same pricing
64	
65	 Remember to enter the EOL deal number when creating the Sitara trade.
66	
67	 Also remember that paths created in Unify assume the stop date is open 
68	ended.  Every effort needs to be made to make sure the appropriate end date 
69	is on the path; otherwise
70	 the number of reconciling items will increase.
71	
72	Please forward this information to anyone else you think might be impacted.
73	
74	Any concerns, please contact Sheri Thomas or myself.
75	
76	SRM (x33548)

bridge from EOL cannot handle this trade.  Because of this, there should be 
heighten attention by Trade Capture given to the EOL Bridge monitor.  These 
trades will error out and will have to be entered manually.

An effort needs to be evaluated and prioritized by both applications (EOL and 
Sitara) on how a deal with multi-periods can flow without human 
intervention.  This has not been started.  In the meantime, a deal of this 
nature will have to be entered manually.

How do I know that a particular deal has multi-period flow?  Once the EOL 
product has been set up, Jennifer and/or Dale will let all involved know.  
The person(s) responsible for entering the deal will have to understand what 
is meant by the EOL product's delivery period and enter the deal 
accordingly.  

For example, assume that a deal has been traded for April:

  Four delivery periods (separate lines) should be included in the Sitara 
ticket
  
  Start: 04/03 Stop: 04/07
   04/10  04/14
   04/17  04/21
   04/24  04/28 
  
 Each delivery period (line) should have the same pricing

 Remember to enter the EOL deal number when creating the Sitara trade.

 Also remember that paths created in Unify assume the stop date is open 
ended.  Every effort needs to be made to make sure the appropriate end date 
is on the path; otherwise
 the number of reconciling items will increase.

Please forward this information to anyone else you think might be impacted.

Any concerns, please contact Sheri Thomas or myself.

SRM (x33548)

content.content:
107	- HL&P month-to-date flow report and shortfall check: Have the system produce the HL&P daily nominated-versus-flowed report, with the 5% tolerance and buyback volumes worked out, instead of a hand-built spreadsheet emailed each week.. Why: The same work is already saved as item 16, 'HL&P month-to-date flow report', which cites all eleven of these update emails plus the 12/99 shortfall thread (683.eml) and the June 2000 resend (1217.eml).
108	- Setting up a new trading book across TAGG, Sitara, RisktRAC/ERMS, CPR and EOL: One routed new-book request form with status tracking and a single completion notice, instead of separate emails to each system's administrator. Why: The routed process already exists: Shona Wilson's memo (giron-d/sent/410.eml, Nov 2000) says one RisktRAC book request form goes to Risk Analysis and Reporting, which forwards it to the ERMS administrator and Global Counterparty and sends a final email to the books list, and says this process had 'formally existed for a number of months'; Giron's own requests from Oct 2000 on (557, 564, 491, 160) are single form submissions to Trevino/McIntyre, so the scattered emails cited come from mid-2000, when people were not following the process, not from how the work runs now. Research that could settle it: Only a new angle could revive it: mail from after Nov 2000 showing that book requests made through the single form still bounce, stall or need follow-up emails to CPR, EOL or Sitara administrators. The steps the form does not cover (the CPR region and EOL trader mapping) would then be a narrower proposal, with its own count of how often it happens.
109	- Settling HPL day/spot deal price and volume disputes: Sitara sends each counterparty a next-morning recap of the prior day's HPL day deals so price and volume mismatches are fixed at once, not at invoicing.. Why: The disputes are a post-sale cleanup: HPL passed to AEP from June 2001 (136.eml, 106.eml 'a deal from when we were at Enron'), every disputed deal is for Dec 2000 to May 2001 production, the earlier mail shows only about three such threads in all of 2000, and several cited threads are not day-deal disputes, so there is no ongoing work at 5 a month for a recap to prevent. Research that could settle it: Find disputes over day deals in Enron's own books after June 2001, outside HPL (for example ENA Texas or other desks' settlements mail), at a steady rate, plus evidence of whether those deals were already confirmed by Enron's Confirmations group; without that the verdict stands.
110	- Upkeep of TW's second, unposted Current Shipper rate matrix: Ask the recipients once whether anyone uses the unposted matrix, and retire it if nobody does.. Why: The archive shows the second matrix being sent only once (29 Oct 2001), and no message says how often Current Shipper rates change, so there is no basis for how often the saving would happen. Research that could settle it: Look for other Current Shipper or Global Settlement rate changes, other TW rate matrix postings, or anything that gives a schedule for those changes (for example, in Rita Bianchi's, Elizabeth Brown's or Jeanette Doll's mail). Two or more dated sends, or a stated schedule, would give a rate.
111	- Building the daily El Paso Electric (EPE) preschedule/schedule sheet: Generate the daily EPE schedule sheet from e-tags and Enpower deals, check it automatically against EPE's dispatch, and phone only the counterparties on the exception list.. Why: The change depends on tag data the mail shows Enron does not get (52.eml: the missing tag did not list EPMIWE, and only EPE's dispatchers had it), the error rate of 8 days a month is about four times what the mail shows, the checkout-call part repeats work already rejected (decisions.md item 60), and 133.eml is a turbine-outage note, not a daily EPE file. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing Enron could read every tag in EPE's control area (for example as EPE's agent on the tagging system) and that the tags exist when the day-ahead sheet is built; count the schedule errors in the EPE sheet over several months; and find anything saying how long preschedule spends building the sheet each day.
112	- Month-end basis and index roll-off calculated twice: Have the risk system produce the 100% basis view and the rolled-off V@R view from one calculation, using a month-end roll-off percentage set centrally.. Why: The same work is already saved as item 3, 'Month-end basis and index roll-off in the gas risk books', which cites the same two messages (giron-d/sent/631.eml and 442.eml) and proposes the same change.
113	- Monthly vacation round and out-of-office coverage notices in Energy Operations / HPL logistics: One shared absence calendar replacing the monthly vacation request round, plus a standing desk-coverage matrix so out-of-office notices go only to backups. Why: The vacation-round half is already saved (decision 24, same calendar, same files 954/1143/1282), and the coverage-notice half rests on miscounted notices and a change that would stop telling the people who need to know who to call. Research that could settle it: A coverage-only proposal would need many more distinct scheduler out-of-office notices across the year, and something in the mail showing that callers went to the wrong person or that notices took real effort to write or re-send. Without that, the savings stay a few minutes a month.
114	- Monthly HPL Assignment, Termination & Expiration report: Generate the report as a scheduled query from the Global Contracts database before each bid week and send it to a self-service subscription list.. Why: The same work is already saved in decisions.md as item 18, 'Monthly HPL Assignment, Termination & Expiration Report', with the same change and the same messages (farmer-d/logistics/211.eml, 2114.eml), so saving it again would count the saving twice.
115	- Monthly TECO Seven Oaks (meter 6884) under/over-take adjustment: Paper the adjustment with TECO and set up standing evergreen purchase and sale deals at meter 6884 so volume management stops asking the desk for deals each month. Why: The account of today's work is out of date: the mail shows standing buy/sell deals (purchase 137870, sale 235670) were set up at meter 6884 after June 2000, and the 2001 stalls come from those deals expiring at 12/00 and from TECO being replaced by El Paso as the counterparty, which an evergreen TECO deal would not fix; the monthly frequency and 42 minutes rest on one request and one remark. Research that could settle it: Restate the work as extending or re-booking the meter 6884 buy/sell deals when they expire or the counterparty changes (corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2093.eml, 2095.eml, 2099.eml, 2149.eml, 2150.eml, 95.eml), count how often that actually happens, and propose a change aimed at that, such as booking the deals for the full term of the lease or plant agreement and rolling them over when the counterparty changes.
116	- Seven Oaks / meter 6884 monthly tailgate adjustment deals: Paper the Seven Oaks adjustment with El Paso (formerly TECO) and book one standing buy/sell deal pair at meter 6884.. Why: The same work is already saved as decisions.md item 22 ('Seven Oaks meter 6884 monthly plant adjustment deals', standing evergreen purchase and sale with El Paso), citing the same files 1626, 194, 2067, 2099 and 95.
117	- Monthly RC allocation % update to commercial teams: Pre-fill each RC's monthly allocation % from the OPM hours survey's commercial-team split, so directors reply only if they disagree.. Why: The allocation file is already sent pre-filled with last month's or preliminary percentages and asks only for changes (862, 1083), and nothing in the mail shows the OPM survey produces per-RC commercial-team percentages that could replace it (1447 shows OPM itself still missing the split), so most of the 520 minutes are not there to save and rest on a guessed 70 managers. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing that OPM's Access tool actually holds hours by commercial team for each RC, on the same team list and month as the Consolidations file, and replies to the allocation file showing how many directors and managers actually change percentages each month and how long it takes them.
118	- Annual budget staffing and salary worksheet: Pre-fill each manager's budget staffing and salary worksheet from an HR/payroll extract by RC. Why: The mail contradicts the estimate: Diane asks managers for only 'a little bit of information', the salary step is a short list of positions with a one-word high/low guess, and she says averages are as accurate as current salaries, so a payroll pre-fill would remove only a few minutes per manager once a year, not 30. Research that could settle it: Look for mail from later budget cycles (2001 for 2002) or from managers showing that the salary and roster step actually took them substantial time, needed several exchanges with Diane, or produced budget errors.
119	- Monthly Investor Relations volumetric variance explanations: Have the monthly Statistical Database refresh list the top counterparty and EOL/non-EOL drivers for each region with a >10% variance, so controllers confirm drivers instead of researching them.. Why: decisions.md has already rejected this work twice for the same gaps, and this version repeats them: nothing in the mail shows that the Statistical Database holds counterparty or EOL detail, or that controllers research drivers by hand (Baumbach's one- and three-line replies name the drivers from memory, the August one the next morning), and the 20-to-8-minute saving for 11 controllers is costed from one controller's replies. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing what the Statistical Database contains (counterparty or EOL breakdowns), replies from controllers other than Baumbach, and requests for other months, showing that working out the drivers takes real lookup time; then cost only that lookup step for the controllers who actually reply.
120	- Double booking of PG&E Texas transport on ENA and an ENA-HPL desk-to-desk deal: Have Legal transfer the ENA PG&E Texas transport contracts to HPL and drop the ENA-HPL desk-to-desk deal, so the transport is scheduled and allocated once.. Group,

Cuts are on the way. While most can be zeroed out in Enpower (for LD's) like normal, longterm contracts will require an annuity for the value of the cut on that particular day. In the interest of being uniform, the guidelines for cuts are below. 

We will be handling cuts in the following manner:

1. Documentation is priority #1. We need to fill out a cut sheet with the times, the name of the person who called, the tag number, the quantity and price.

2. After attempting to resupply the cut or find an alternate sink we need to carefully document changes in the new enpower workspace.

3. We need to zero out all cut deals in Enpower, we then need to calculate the value of the deals and make an annuity. The annuity must be made HE 1 on the following day of the schedule. The annuity needs to be for 1 mw for the value of the zeroed out contract. In the comment section of the annuity you must include the Enpower deal # of the cut deal and should include an indication of the number of mws each hour and the contract price--for example (4 hours @ 25 mws X $100 per mw = $10,000).

4. Please be as accurate as possible. We still need to be flat in Enpower at the end of each day. And we still need to calculate our daily position.

5. Put all cut sheets in the accordion folder on Kate Symes' Desk.

I appreciate your help and diligence.
Thanks,

Bill
